decisive_quotes.quote: (D) Any member of that household is ineligible under § 273.11(m) by virtue of a conviction for a drug-related felony, ... or under § 273.11(s) for having a conviction of certain crimes and not being in compliance with the sentence.

provision_review.why: 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)(D) says one member must both have the conviction and be out of compliance with the sentence. The pre-fix rule ANDed two separate household-wide facts (some member convicted, some member noncompliant), so it fires when member A is convicted and member B is noncompliant. The post-fix rule tests the conjunction for each member and then aggregates. provision.txt (WIC 18901.5) does not mention these bars.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)(D) bars a household when 'any member' is ineligible '[under] § 273.11(s) for having a conviction of certain crimes and not being in compliance with the sentence' — a conjunction predicated of one member — but the pre-fix module evaluated that conjunction at Household entity over two separate household-wide existential facts, so a conviction held by member A combined with sentence noncompliance by member B (a split witness) wrongly denied the whole household MCE.
triage.triage_notes: Provision read: I resolved us/regulation/7/273/2 through the pinned corpus and confirmed (vii)(A)/(D) are 'any member' tests, (B) is 'the entire household is disqualified ... workfare', and (C) is 'the head of the household'. The fix re-levels entity Household -> Person on calfresh_wic_18901_3_drug_felony_opt_out_applies, calfresh_mce_federal_drug_felony_exclusion_before_state_opt_out, and the renamed calfresh_mce_member_household_exclusion_applies, then aggregates with count_where(calfresh_mce_member_of_household, ...) > 0 in the household-level rule that takes over the old name calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies; note the rename shuffle (old calfresh_mce_drug_felony_exclusion_applies deleted, old calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies renamed to ..._member_household_...), so diff line matching is misleading without reading both file versions. Decisive evidence is the new companion case 'different_members_cannot_split_serious_crime_conviction_and_sentence_noncompliance' (member 1 has the conviction, member 2 is out of compliance, expected calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies: not_holds), which the pre-fix formula would have failed; two more new cases (federal_drug_felony_member_exclusion_exists_before_the_state_opt_out, member_ipv_bar_applies_before_household_aggregation) pin the member-level layer. PROGRESS.md in the same commit states verbatim: 'Moved all member-triggered paragraph-(vii) bars to `Person` scope and aggregates them through the MCE household relation; only the whole-household workfare bar remains a direct household fact. This both matches source scope and prevents split-witness false positives.' — I did not use it as description_quote because PROGRESS.md is not one of the allowed quote sources; the commit subject's 'source scope' is the in-scope paraphrase of the same thing. Secondary changes bundled here: the added upstream_source_check block (provenance, mechanical), one proof atom moved between rules, and removal of the intermediate calfresh_mce_drug_felony_exclusion_applies, described in PROGRESS.md as 'Removed the unreachable current-law effective drug-felony intermediate' — that removal is behaviour-neutral today because calfresh_wic_18901_3_drug_felony_opt_out_applies is the constant `true`, so the drug-felony branch was and remains dead under current California law; the live defect corrected is the serious-crime split witness. Single-predicate bars (IPV, monthly reporting, fleeing felon, probation/parole) and the head-of-household work bar are semantically unchanged by the re-leveling. An alternative kind of polarity_or_logic is defensible (any(A) and any(B) vs any(A and B)), but the entity fields literally changed and the message says 'scope', so wrong_entity_or_scope is the better fit.
triage.verifier_justification: The pinned corpus text of 7 CFR 273.2(j)(2)(vii)(D) predicates its whole disjunction of "Any member of that household," so the final disjunct "having a conviction of certain crimes and not being in compliance with the sentence" is a conjunction about one member; the pre-fix module evaluated it at entity: Household as the AND of two independent household-wide existential inputs (household_member_has_serious_crime_conviction and household_member_not_in_compliance_with_serious_crime_sentence), which fires on a split witness. The fix changes entity: Household to entity: Person on three rules, renames the rule to calfresh_mce_member_household_exclusion_applies, evaluates the conjunction per member, and aggregates with count_where(calfresh_mce_member_of_household, ...) > 0, while the household rule retains only the genuinely household-level (vii)(B) workfare bar. The commit adds the regression test different_members_cannot_split_serious_crime_conviction_and_sentence_noncompliance, whose two-member fixture (A convicted, B noncompliant) expects calfresh_mce_household_exclusion_applies: not_holds, which is exactly the case the old encoding got wrong. The and/or operators and negations are unchanged, so this is a member-set/entity scope correction rather than polarity_or_logic, and it is not mechanical because formulas, entities, and input scope all changed.
triage.verifier_notes: Verified against the pinned release (corpus_release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, corpus_commit 0fd35bfbda98836c406ec539a492c4e661c6695d, provision us/regulation/7/273/2): "(D) Any member of that household is ineligible under § 273.11(m) ... or under § 273.11(s) for having a conviction of certain crimes and not being in compliance with the sentence." Refutations tried and rejected: (1) mechanical — no, `entity: Household` -> `entity: Person` on calfresh_wic_18901_3_drug_felony_opt_out_applies, calfresh_mce_federal_drug_felony_exclusion_before_state_opt_out, and the renamed member rule, plus formula rewrites; the upstream_source_check block is only the metadata part of the diff. (2) not_a_defect/new coverage — no, the pre-fix rule already carried a proof atom quoting the exact § 273.11(s) clause, so the module claimed that meaning. (3) polarity_or_logic — no operator was inverted or recombined; only the quantification entity changed, and the kind list explicitly places "household member set" under wrong_entity_or_scope; the commit subject is "fix(ca): validate CalFresh MCE source scope". Scoping caveat for the corpus: the serious-crime conjunction is the ONLY clause whose truth value actually changes. The IPV/monthly-reporting/fleeing-felon/probation clauses are disjunctions of existentials and flatten equivalently; the head-of-household clause becomes member_is_household_head and member_disqualified_for_work_requirement_noncompliance, equivalent to the old household-level input; the drug-felony branch is inert in both versions because calfresh_wic_18901_3_drug_felony_opt_out_applies has `formula: true` before and after; and the (vii)(B) workfare clause is correctly hoisted to the household rule since the source says "The entire household is disqualified". Anchor the corpus entry on rules[calfresh_mce_member_household_exclusion_applies].versions[0].formula (serious-crime conjunction), which matches the first reader's rule_path. Separately: module index 0 of this same commit (us-ca/policies/cdss/snap/fy-2026-benefit-calculation.yaml) adds nothing but the upstream_source_check metadata block and should be scored mechanical if scored as its own case. All commands run were read-only (git show, cat, sed, grep on a single file, resolve_provision.py).
